summary: Hideyuki Matsumori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied as a doctoral student at Soka University (attested 2006) and was later an assistant professor (助教) there, attested in 2015.

Hildegard Diemberger works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under the supervision of Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner, and her students include Michela Clemente, Lobsang Yongdan, and Adrian Zenz.

Himanshu Prabha Ray is an Indologist and historian/archaeologist educated at Panjab University, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. She was Associate Professor at JNU (~1980–2012) and Chairperson of the National Monuments Authority (~2012–2015), among other appointments.

Hinrich Middeldorpf (1788–1861) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. Educated at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the University of Göttingen (~1807–1811), he held a post at the University of Breslau (~1813–1861) and taught Albrecht Weber.

Hiralal Rasikdas Kapadia (b. 1894) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. In 1947, he was attested as Professor of Ardhamagadhi at MTB Arts College and as a Ph.D. teacher in Ardhamagadhi at the University of Mumbai.

Hiram W. Woodward (b. 1940) specializes in art history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Harvard and Yale, he taught at the University of Michigan (1972–1982) and was curator of Asian art at the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned degrees from Oriental College, Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College, and Panjab University. He served as Government Epigraphist (attested 1931) and Director of Archaeology for Baroda State (1934–1942).
Hiroaki Yokoyama works in Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2013) and later held an appointment there as a research student (研究生).

Hirofumi Isoda (b. 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his doctoral studies at Tohoku University by 1966. He served as Associate Professor at Tohoku University (attested 1989–2000) and Professor Emeritus at Shimane University (attested 1974).

Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He was a professor at Tokushima University (~1974–2002) and a special researcher at Rissho University (attested 1985).
Hiroko Kawanami works in Buddhist studies and religious studies, having studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott. She served as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).
Hiroko Matsuoka is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and held a post at the University of Leipzig (attested 2016).

Hiromasa Tosaki (b. 1930) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Kyushu University, studied at Harvard, and served as a professor at Kyushu University (~1978–1994) after teaching at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College.
Hiromi Habata (b. 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg (~1990–2004) and held a research post at the University of Munich (~2005).

Hiromi Yoshimura (b. 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Ryukoku University, including full-time lecturer (attested 1987) and another post attested in 2006, and taught Nobumichi Kusumoto.
Hiromu Kitanishi (1925–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University (~1945–1950) and later served there as a professor (~1969–1991).
Hironari Tanaka works in Buddhist studies. He was a PhD student at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020) and also held a post there.

Hiroo Kashiwagi (b. 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at Matsusaka University (~1982–1998) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College (~1989–1997).

Hiroo Sato (b. 1953) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tohoku University (~1972–1981), he taught at Morioka College (~1988–1993) and was a professor at Tohoku University (~2001–2019).

Hiroshi Aoyagi (b. 1957) specializes in linguistics and Japanology. Educated at International Christian University and the University of Southern California (PhD 1998), he became a professor at Nanzan University (~1999).
